result: h07. The browser hits `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`. The URL itself is minted server-side: `convertUserFromStore` rewrites a base64 avatar into that path so the API response stays small (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:32-40`), and `UserAvatar.tsx` just renders it as an `` (`web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14`). Main path: - `RegisterRoutes` (route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125 - `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 - `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 - `Store.GetUser` — store/user.go:148 - `Store.ListUsers` — store/user.go:136 - `(*DB).ListUsers` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (mirrored at store/db/mysql/user.go:84, store/db/postgres/user.go:87) - `SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user WHERE username = ?` → `rows.Scan(&user.AvatarURL)` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:151-197 - `FileServerService.parseDataURI` (decodes the `data:image/…;base64,…` column value) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 - `c.Blob(http.StatusOK, imageType, imageData)` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209 Conditional auth hop, taken only when the instance is private (`!s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()`, fileserver.go:173): - `FileServerService.getCurrentUser` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 - `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` — server/auth/authenticator.go:190 Two things worth noting about where the data actually lives: - Avatar bytes are **not** in attachment storage (no local file / S3 / blob branch like `serveAttachmentFile` has). They're stored inline in the `user.avatar_url` column as a base64 data URI, so the "data layer" terminates at that column scan. - The `userCache` in `Store.GetUser` is bypassed here: it's only consulted when `find.ID != nil` (store/user.go:149), and this lookup is by `Username`, so every avatar request reaches the DB driver. Authorization detail: past the private-instance gate there is no per-user check — any authenticated viewer (or any anonymous visitor on a public instance) can fetch any user's avatar by username. That appears intentional, matching the test `TestServeUserAvatar_PrivateInstanceRequiresAuth` (server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:508).
